keyChanges.title: Musk expects AI5 in Optimus around April 2027; Taylor still trial-only
keyChanges.description: On the 21 October 2026 Q3 earnings call, recapped by Not a Tesla App on 22 October, Elon Musk said he expects AI5 to be integrated into Optimus around April 2027. He again described AI5 as an order of magnitude more compute than AI4, and said AI5 entered trial production at Samsung’s Texas fab in September. The call gave no vehicle AI5 date, no yield, and no unit count. Taylor Fab 1 is still in tool qualification, and 2nm volume remains a 2027 event, so the April 2027 robot date sits inside the same year the foundry is supposed to leave trial production. FC-BGA substrates tied to these AI chips are scheduled to reach Tesla in 2029. The same recap’s in-house fab schedule belongs to the terafab category.

positive_signals: First named product-integration date for AI5: Optimus around April 2027
Call restates roughly 10x AI4 compute and confirms September trial production at Samsung’s Texas fab
negative_signals: Wording is an expectation, with no sampled vehicle computer, yield, or unit count
No AI5 date for cars
Taylor remains pre-volume and 2nm volume is still 2027, so April 2027 is inside the year volume is supposed to start
Substrate deliveries for these AI chips start in 2029, after the robot date
Tesla IR transcript was not opened; confidence rests on one detailed call recap

keyChanges.title: Tesla reportedly prepays KRW 1.1T for FC-BGA that arrives in 2029
keyChanges.description: Maeil Business Newspaper, via TrendForce on 22 October 2026, with the same split in Crypto Briefing and a Digitimes lede, says Tesla is committing about KRW 1.1 trillion and Nvidia about KRW 2.6 trillion (KRW 3.7 trillion combined, about US$2.8 billion) so Samsung Electro-Mechanics can build FC-BGA substrate lines. Tesla’s piece is a five-year supply contract for AI-chip substrates used in autonomous vehicles and Optimus, covering 2029–2033. Sejong construction is expected to finish at the end of 2027, equipment and trial production in the first half of 2028, mass production in the second half of 2028, and first deliveries to Tesla in 2029. That reserves packaging capacity. It misses both the April 2027 Optimus AI5 claim and Taylor’s 2027 volume target. The KRW 1.1 trillion figure is a reported capacity prepayment, and the US$2.8 billion headline is joint with Nvidia. A separate SEMCO memory-substrate contract of KRW 360.5 billion announced 19 October is to an unnamed customer.

positive_signals: Tesla is paying to reserve dedicated FC-BGA capacity for 2029–2033 rather than a spot purchase order
Nvidia’s larger check and its 21 October GTC Germany backing show the substrate bottleneck is real and SEMCO is building lines for it
Sejong schedule is specific: construction end-2027, trial 1H 2028, mass production 2H 2028
negative_signals: Tesla has not confirmed the contract in an IR filing; the figure comes from Maeil via TrendForce, Crypto Briefing, and Digitimes
Tesla’s KRW 1.1 trillion is the smaller check; Nvidia is about KRW 2.6 trillion
First Tesla deliveries are 2029, after the April 2027 Optimus AI5 claim and after the 2027 Taylor volume target
The lines are shared with Nvidia, so this is not Tesla-dedicated output
US$2.8 billion is the combined figure and is not a chip-production count

key_metrics.actual: Reported KRW 1.1T Tesla FC-BGA prepay; deliveries 2029
key_metrics.target: AI5 Optimus integration around April 2027; Samsung 2nm volume in 2027
key_metrics.trajectory: Packaging supply lands after both near-term chip dates

keyChanges.title: Intel names Tesla a 14A foundry customer; chip, price, and wafers unspecified
keyChanges.description: Around 19 October 2026, secondary reports said Intel named Tesla as a customer for its 14A process, a 1.4nm-class node aimed at about 2028. Not a Tesla App’s 24 October write-up says the chip is unnamed, carries no dollar value or wafer volume, and is distinct from AI4+. Intel’s 14A timing is later than AI5, which stays on Samsung 2nm (trial now, volume still 2027) and TSMC 3nm. Finviz tied the same-day Intel share move to a JPMorgan upgrade and an 18A progress comment as well as the Tesla agreement. AInvest frames the disclosure as economically small external foundry work and links 14A to the earlier in-house fab plan, which conflicts with Not a Tesla App’s reading that Intel would run the wafers in Intel fabs. Either reading leaves 2026–2027 AI5 supply on Samsung and TSMC. No Intel investor-relations page was opened.

positive_signals: Secondary reports name Tesla as an Intel 14A foundry customer, the first named external 14A logo in this coverage
If the wafers are actually run in Intel fabs, it would be a later-decade source beside Samsung and TSMC
negative_signals: Chip name, contract value, and wafer volume are absent
14A is a ~2028 node and does not change AI5’s Samsung 2nm / TSMC 3nm plan or Taylor’s 2027 volume
Same-day Intel share move also followed a JPMorgan upgrade and an 18A progress comment
AInvest’s account may restate the earlier 14A in-house-fab comment rather than a new inference-chip purchase order
AInvest puts Intel external foundry sales near $293 million inside a $5.8 billion quarterly foundry total that is mostly internal transfers
No Intel IR primary was opened

keyChanges.title: Q3 still lists Texas 4680 above 40 GWh and prints no cell output
keyChanges.description: Tesla's Q3 2026 update, released for the Oct. 21 earnings call, again says battery availability limited how fast auto volume grew in the quarter, and that the company is still increasing 4680 production for Cybercab, Tesla Semi, and higher Model Y volumes. The cell-capacity table is unchanged from the Q2 2026 update: Texas 4680 installed capacity above 40 GWh with status Production, Texas cathode materials 10 GWh Early Ramp, Texas lithium refining 30 GWh Early Ramp, and Berlin 4680 still Construction with no capacity figure. The same footnote says installed capacity is not the production rate. Tesla published no yield, no cells produced, and no actual 4680 GWh output. The first Megapacks built with Nevada LFP cells are an energy-storage milestone, not a 4680 ramp.

positive_signals: Shareholder letter says Tesla continues to increase 4680 production for Cybercab, Semi, and higher Model Y volumes
Texas 4680 line remains labeled Production, with installed capacity still listed above 40 GWh
Letter says Tesla made additional progress securing future battery supply
negative_signals: No yield, cell count, or actual GWh produced; the above-40 GWh figure is installed capacity, and the footnote says that is not the production rate
Table matches Q2 2026 exactly: Texas 4680 above 40 GWh Production, cathode 10 GWh Early Ramp, lithium refining 30 GWh Early Ramp, Berlin 4680 still Construction with a dash for capacity
Battery availability continued to be the limiting factor on auto volume in the quarter
Berlin's 4680 line has not left construction and still has no stated capacity

keyChanges.title: Cybercab's 4680 pack is built to switch to LFP later
keyChanges.description: On a Munro Live Cybercab tour reported Oct. 26-27, Tesla pack director Robert Sumpf said the pack uses the company's own nickel 4680 cells today in an 88S6P layout (528 cells) and that empty space beside and under the modules was left so Tesla can move to a lower-energy-density chemistry and bring LFP onto the platform as volume scales. Lars Moravy said part of that space exists because the car did not need as many cells as Tesla expected. The pack is four individually sealed modules in a case, not the glued structural pack used on some Model Ys; Sumpf graded the Model Y structural pack a D on service cost and said a fully structural pack adds about 10 percent cell volume that is not worth the repair cost. No LFP date, cell supplier, range impact, or confirmed pack kWh was given. A 2025 target of under 50 kWh was cited and not updated.

positive_signals: Cybercab currently runs Tesla's in-house nickel 4680 cells, confirmed as an 88S6P pack (528 cells) by Drive Tesla Canada and Teslarati's account of the tour
Four sealed modules can be replaced individually, which Tesla says cuts service cost versus a glued structural pack on a high-mileage robotaxi
Spare volume is an intentional chemistry option, not an accident of packaging
negative_signals: Sumpf said the pack was protected so Tesla can bring LFP in as it scales; no timing, supplier, or range figure
Moravy said Tesla needed fewer cells than it had planned, so 4680 content per Cybercab is already smaller than the original design
The structural 4680 pack, the original density bet, was not used; Sumpf graded the Model Y structural pack a D
The Q3 letter says 4680 output is meant to support the Cybercab ramp, but this pack is engineered to leave nickel 4680
Pack energy is still unpublished; the under-50 kWh figure is an early-2025 target, not a confirmed spec

keyChanges.title: Cybercab line sits idle some days because deployment cannot absorb output
keyChanges.description: On October 26 Lars Moravy told Munro Live, on the Giga Texas line, that Tesla does not run the Cybercab line every day because it is building faster than the company can put cars into service: 'Right now the manufacturing line's ahead.' That revises the October 21 earnings-call framing, where Moravy said production was racing to keep up with autonomous miles and that the deck's listed capacity of more than 125,000 units a year is only a rate the line can run today, with a higher unnamed ceiling. CFO Vaibhav Taneja said the harder problem is regulatory approval so Tesla can deploy Cybercabs as fast as it builds them. The tour also showed the line at about 78% automation against a 10-second, 100% automation target, 25 final stations, no paint shop, and no tear-down car released to Munro. Tesla still has not published a unit-built count. Every Cybercab built so far is going into Tesla's own fleet, and the only on-road Cybercab concentration shown this week was 50-plus cars at the Austin F1 weekend.

positive_signals: Moravy says the unboxed line can run faster than the >125,000-unit listed annual rate and uses about half the parts and half the floor space of other Teslas
Final assembly is 25 automated stations and the framing line is described as fully automated
negative_signals: The line is intentionally not run every day because deployment is the bottleneck, so nameplate speed is not output
Taneja said regulatory approvals, not the factory, limit how fast Cybercabs can enter service
78% automation versus a 100% / 10-second goal, and Tesla disclosed no production total
All units still go to Tesla's own fleet; customer cars and a second city are still ahead of the cars already built

keyChanges.title: Robotaxi safety page claims 3.1 million miles and names four cities with no dates
keyChanges.description: On October 21 Tesla published a Robotaxi safety page covering January 22 through October 18. It claims 3.1 million miles with no safety monitor in the car, zero injuries, zero airbag deployments, and zero pedestrian or cyclist impacts, and it lists Las Vegas, Jacksonville, Phoenix, and San Antonio as coming soon with no launch dates and no statement on whether those cities start with a safety monitor. City miles are concentrated and uneven: Austin 2,118,015, Dallas 608,130, Houston 225,964, Orlando 61,053, Tampa 53,117, Miami 46,262. The Bay Area is omitted because a safety driver is still required. TeslaNorth notes the mile total includes trips where a remote operator assisted or took over, and the page does not publish the count of minor collisions filed under NHTSA's Standing General Order. The Q3 shareholder letter, for the quarter ended September 30, separately said nearly 2 million cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles, so the October 18 figure is a company series with a different cutoff and, on TeslaNorth's reading, a wider definition. The human-driver comparison (about 9.1 injury crashes over the same miles) is Tesla's own calculation against Texas police data. The open school-zone defect petition is not resolved by a zero-injury claim.

positive_signals: Tesla's own page reports 3.1 million no-monitor miles through October 18 and zero claimed injuries, airbag deployments, or vulnerable-road-user impacts
Austin plus Dallas account for most of the miles, and the Q3 letter said unsupervised Robotaxi miles grew about eightfold in the quarter to nearly 2 million by September 30
negative_signals: Miles include remote-operator assist and takeover trips, monitored rides are excluded, and minor crash counts are not shown
Four named cities have no dates; Florida cities are still tens of thousands of miles, not a scaled network
San Francisco Bay Area remains safety-monitor-only and is left out of the autonomous total
The school-zone defect petition is still open; a company safety page is not a regulator finding

keyChanges.title: Cybercab Dallas launch is a November promise, not a start of service
keyChanges.description: On the October 21 earnings call Ashok Elluswamy said there is no fundamental reason Cybercab stays in Austin and that 'next month we'll be launching in Dallas,' with the same software then meant to scale alongside Model Y robotaxis. CFO Vaibhav Taneja was more cautious the same day: Cybercab is available only in Austin today, and Tesla plans to bring it to some other cities before year-end, without naming them. Dallas already has unsupervised Model Y Robotaxi service, with 608,130 no-monitor miles on Tesla's safety page through October 18, so a Cybercab launch there would be a vehicle swap or add, not a new city. As of October 31 no outlet has reported Cybercab rides open in Dallas. Headlines that Cybercab has 'hit' Dallas describe a sentence on a call, not operating service.

positive_signals: Elluswamy gave a dated plan: Cybercab service in Dallas in November 2026, the first city outside Austin
Dallas already runs driverless Model Y robotaxis, so the software and a service area exist
negative_signals: Taneja said Cybercab rides are Austin-only today
November has not started and no Dallas Cybercab service is live
Model Y miles in Dallas are not Cybercab deployment

keyChanges.title: Year-end Cybercab customer deliveries are an aim, and most cars stay Tesla-owned
keyChanges.description: On the October 21 call Lars Moravy said Tesla is 'trying to get Cybercabs to customers by the end of this year, 2026,' starting small, while every car built so far still goes to the internal Robotaxi fleet. Elon Musk said the vast majority of Cybercabs will be Tesla-owned transport-as-a-service, not a personal car like Model 3 or Model Y. There is no public order page, no price confirmation against the old roughly $30,000 talk, and no named first buyer. The NHTSA audit query on how a car with no steering wheel or pedals was self-certified (AQ26002) was still the open constraint: sworn answers were due October 30, and as of this pass no Tier 1 outlet has reported a filing or a closed audit. A line that already outruns deployment makes a late-2026 retail handoff a logistics and certification problem, not evidence that sales have opened.

positive_signals: Moravy put a year-end 2026 target on the first customer Cybercabs and said initial deliveries would be used to learn ownership and fleet handoff
A business interest form for future Cybercab fleet purchases was already up before this call
negative_signals: Wording is 'trying,' not a delivery start, and Musk said the vast majority stay Tesla-owned
All current production is still internal fleet
AQ26002 self-certification audit was unanswered in public coverage through the October 30 due date
No order book, no confirmed transaction, and two months left in 2026

keyChanges.title: Austin Robotaxi hours move to 2 a.m., still four hours short of 24/7
keyChanges.description: Not a Tesla App reported on October 30 that Tesla's Robotaxi account listed operating hours of 6 a.m. to 2 a.m., a 20-hour day. That follows the October 17 midnight cutoff and an October 22 rider screenshot of a 1 a.m. last call limited to nearby drop-offs around F1 weekend. On the October 21 call Elluswamy had said 2 a.m. was coming 'pretty soon' and that 24/7 operation, higher-speed roads, more weather, and highways were hoped for by year-end. The October 30 write-up says Tesla did not say which cities get the 2 a.m. cutoff or whether it is Cybercab-only. Q3 materials the same week as the call still described Austin as 6 a.m. to midnight. Round-the-clock service is still a year-end aim, not the current schedule. Calm Mode and a rear camera view shipped in the same window; they do not change hours or fleet size.

positive_signals: Hours stepped from midnight to a stated 6 a.m.–2 a.m. window within two weeks, matching the near-term line Elluswamy gave on the earnings call
Night miles were already 862,000 of the 3.1 million on the safety page through October 18
negative_signals: Service is still dark for four hours; 24/7 is not in effect
Tesla did not specify cities, and the prior 1 a.m. app state was limited to nearby drop-offs

keyChanges.title: Texas authorization roster hits 1,051 vehicles; that is not the dispatch fleet
keyChanges.description: Texas DMV / TxMCCS records reviewed by TeslaNorth on October 27 list 1,051 authorized 2026 vehicles for Tesla Robotaxi, LLC: 544 Cybercabs and 507 Model Ys. That is the first time Cybercab is the majority of the authorization list. Since an October 9 snapshot of 319 Cybercabs and 739 vehicles total, the roster added 225 Cybercabs and 87 Model Ys. The same pages list VIN, year, make, and model only. They do not show which cars are in Austin versus sitting in Dallas or Houston, or how many carried a paying rider that day. A Saturday tracker count cited by TeslaNorth put registered Cybercabs at 463 before the Tuesday pull. Registration under the Texas automated-vehicle list is the legal ceiling, not a production print and not an active Robotaxi fleet count. The on-road evidence the same weekend was a spotter count of more than 50 Cybercabs at Circuit of the Americas.

positive_signals: Authorized Cybercabs rose from 319 on October 9 to 544 on October 27, crossing Model Y on the Texas roster
Tesla Robotaxi, LLC has held Authorized status since May 14, 2026, so the added VINs are on the commercial credential, not a private demo list
negative_signals: TxMCCS does not disclose how many of the 544 Cybercabs are in paid service
The largest same-week on-road Cybercab grouping reported was 50-plus at F1, an order of magnitude below the roster
Moravy said the factory is already ahead of deployment, so more registrations do not equal more rides

keyChanges.title: Houston Robotaxi map grows sharply; Cybercab is still not in service there
keyChanges.description: On October 26 Tesla's Robotaxi account posted that a bigger Houston service area was live, stretching from the old northwest patch through downtown toward Bellaire and the edge of Pasadena. Musk quote-posted the rocket-shaped map. Not a Tesla App, measuring the geofence, put the zone at about 254 square miles versus about 25 before, covering on the order of 1.2 million residents, and said both Houston airports remain outside it. Tesla did not publish square miles or a change in hours. Rides in Houston are still unsupervised Model Y, not Cybercab. The safety page had Houston at 225,964 no-monitor miles through October 18, far behind Austin and Dallas, so the map grew ahead of demonstrated utilization. Cybercab commercial rides in Houston were not announced.

positive_signals: Tesla's Robotaxi account confirmed a larger Houston geofence is live, the first Houston expansion since the April Model Y launch
Tracker measurement puts the zone near 254 square miles, several times a mapped Waymo Houston area of about 49 square miles
negative_signals: Houston's no-monitor miles through October 18 were 225,964, the smallest of the three Texas cities
Airports are still outside the zone, and Tesla gave no area or hours figure of its own

keyChanges.title: Austin F1 weekend showed 50-plus Cybercabs, not a fleet-size print
keyChanges.description: On October 25 Tesla's Robotaxi account posted 'Swarm' and Ashok Elluswamy reposted a photo of Cybercabs and Model Y robotaxis lined up near Circuit of the Americas during the United States Grand Prix. Riders and spotters counted more than 50 Cybercabs by midday. The Austin geofence had been stretched to the track on October 22, when a rider app also showed a 1 a.m. last call limited to nearby drop-offs; some track-adjacent pins were marked service blocked, and one rider said the drop was a walk of under 20 minutes from the gate. Cybercab Spotter logged 1,250 Austin Cybercab sightings on qualifying Saturday versus 1,072 on October 16; sightings count the same car more than once and are not a fleet census. Tesla has not published ride totals, wait times, or whether the COTA boundary stays after the race. Waymo's Austin area, via Uber, did not cover the track.

positive_signals: Tesla and its AI lead publicly showed a large Cybercab and Model Y grouping working an event surge at COTA
The geofence was extended to the circuit before the race weekend, beyond Waymo's Austin coverage
negative_signals: More than 50 cars at the track is a spotter count, not a network fleet size, and it sits far below the Texas authorization roster
Tesla published no ride count or wait time, and some drop-offs were short of the gate
Tesla has not said the COTA boundary or the temporary late last-call rules remain after the event

keyChanges.title: Dallas and Houston comp the first Robotaxi ride; Austin does not
keyChanges.description: On October 28–29 the Robotaxi app showed 'First ride on us' and a $0.00 fare for new riders in Dallas and Houston, according to tracker Ethan McKanna and write-ups at TeslaNorth and Not a Tesla App. Austin, the only Cybercab city, did not show the promo in his checks. Tesla's corporate and Robotaxi accounts had not posted the offer. Houston's map had just been enlarged and Dallas is the city named for a November Cybercab start, so the comp lands in markets Tesla is trying to fill, not in the busiest one. On the earnings call Taneja said the 30-cent-per-mile Robotaxi cost target is still a goal, not a result. A free first trip is a ridership tactic; it is not evidence that paid demand is covering the cars.

positive_signals: Two outlets independently reported the same in-app $0 first-ride state in Dallas and Houston
The offer is limited to a first trip, not a standing fare cut
negative_signals: Tesla has not confirmed the promo, and it is absent in Austin where Cybercab actually runs
Comped rides in the expansion cities are a demand push, while the 30-cent-per-mile target remains unmet
Dallas Cybercab service itself is still not open

keyChanges.title: NHTSA proposes optional cyan lamps for cars with no steering wheel
keyChanges.description: NHTSA posted a proposed change to FMVSS 108, slated for Federal Register publication on October 26, that would let vehicles without manual driving controls use automated turn signals, hazards, and high beams, and that would allow optional steady cyan marker lamps (up to eight) only when no human is expected to watch the road. Tesla is not named. The rule is a proposal with a 30-day comment period, not a final standard, and it does not answer FMVSS 135's foot-brake requirement or close audit query AQ26002. NHTSA said that without changes like these, makers of pedal-free cars would keep seeking exemptions. Mercedes-Benz, not Tesla, is the company cited as having tested cyan lamps. The proposal is a paperwork path for the Cybercab's lighting and signal controls; it is not approval to scale the vehicle.

positive_signals: The proposal would drop manual signal-cancel and high-beam hand controls for vehicles that have no driver controls, which matches the Cybercab layout
NHTSA called the change deregulatory and said it does not expect added cost
negative_signals: It is an optional lighting proposal, Tesla is unnamed, and comments are still open
It does not resolve the brake-pedal standard or the open Cybercab certification audit
Cyan lamps are not required, so the rule does not by itself put a visible autonomy marker on the Austin fleet

keyChanges.title: Vallejo I-80 Pedestrian Killed; Driver Told CHP the Tesla Was on FSD
keyChanges.description: Around 2:35 a.m. on 22 October, a 71-year-old man was killed while crossing westbound Interstate 80 at the I-780 interchange in Vallejo. The 26-year-old San Francisco driver stayed at the scene and told California Highway Patrol his Tesla was in Full Self-Driving. CHP said it reviewed the car's dashcam: the Tesla was in the second lane at about 70 mph when the man walked in from the right shoulder toward the center divider; the video shows the brakes applied and the car steered left, and the right front still struck him. CHP also said at least one later vehicle hit him in the lanes and did not stop. This is a separate crash from the 13 October Fairfield collision with a CHP car. Headlines calling the car 'self-driving' overstate a supervised system, and CHP's account is the driver's statement plus dashcam, not a Tesla telemetry release or a new NHTSA case file. A freeway pedestrian death with FSD claimed engaged is still a safety failure of the product as used.

positive_signals: The driver remained at the scene and gave CHP the dashcam
CHP said the video shows braking and a left steer before impact, not a no-reaction strike
negative_signals: A pedestrian died after the driver told CHP the Tesla was in Full Self-Driving
Avoidance still ended in a right-front strike at about 70 mph
A second unidentified vehicle also struck the man and left
This is the second I-80 crash in nine days in which a driver put FSD in the story, after the Fairfield CHP-car collision
No public Tesla log or NHTSA opening was attached to this crash in the reporting

key_metrics.actual: 1 pedestrian killed; Tesla ~70 mph; FSD claimed by driver
key_metrics.target: Supervised system with the driver preventing a fatal strike
key_metrics.trajectory: Second Bay Area I-80 FSD-claimed crash in nine days; no new federal case announced

keyChanges.title: Seoul Police Book 80 People for Illegal Tesla FSD Unlocks
keyChanges.description: On 27 October the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said it had booked 80 people under the Motor Vehicle Management Act for switching on Full Self-Driving with unauthorized devices, and seized 21 devices. Suspects imported modules from Europe and China or built their own, including one made from GitHub material, and some traded tips on keeping the activation off the car's records. Police said safety risks were confirmed, including FSD failing to read conditions or behaving differently from the driver's intent. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport asked for the investigation in April. The legal gap is the point: FSD is authorized only on U.S.-built Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck under the Korea-U.S. FTA certification exemption. China-built Model 3 and Model Y, the volume cars, have not passed Korea's safety standards for the feature. Korea JoongAng Daily, citing Carisyou Data Lab, said only 47,458 of 229,311 Teslas on Korean roads as of August, 20.7 percent, can legally use it. That is a market-research count, not a ministry certification total. Maximum exposure cited by police is two years in prison or a 20 million won fine, about $15,000. Booking is not a conviction, and it does not open a legal path for Shanghai-built cars.

positive_signals: Police and the transport ministry are enforcing the certification line instead of ignoring a gray market
U.S.-built Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck remain a legal supervised-FSD path in Korea
negative_signals: China-built Model 3 and Model Y still have not cleared Korean safety standards for FSD
JoongAng, citing Carisyou, puts legal availability at 20.7 percent of the Korean Tesla fleet
Owners are importing or building unlock hardware and sharing ways to hide logs
Police described confirmed safety risks from unauthorized software
The crackdown does not certify the cars people are trying to unlock

key_metrics.actual: 80 people booked; 21 devices seized; 20.7% of Korean Teslas cited as legally eligible
key_metrics.target: Certified supervised FSD on the cars Tesla actually sells in volume in Korea
key_metrics.trajectory: Enforcement up, certification of China-built cars still closed

keyChanges.title: Latvia Recognizes Dutch FSD Approval, Tenth EU State, Still No Dated Rollout
keyChanges.description: On 26 October Tesla Europe posted that Tesla Assisted Driving, the European name for FSD (Supervised), is approved in Latvia and that rollout begins soon, with no date. Teslarati reported that Latvia's Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD) evaluated the Dutch RDW file from the 10 April provisional approval, coordinated with other authorities, and reviewed Tesla changes: tighter speed-offset limits, automatic reset of manual speed adjustments after each trip, and stronger driver monitoring. The running recognition list is now the Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, Czechia, Croatia, Slovakia, and Latvia. It is still SAE Level 2. The driver must monitor the road and be ready to intervene. Most of these clearances are mutual recognition of one Dutch provisional approval, not a fresh national test program. An EU-wide authorization still needs a qualified majority in the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles, at least 15 of 27 states representing 65 percent of the EU population. Germany, France, and Italy remain under review. A December vote is described as expected, not held. Latvia is another small-state checkbox. It does not put the feature on cars, and it does not supply the population weight the vote requires.

positive_signals: Tesla Europe said Latvia is approved and CSDD reviewed the Dutch file plus Tesla's speed-offset, reset, and driver-monitoring changes
Tenth EU recognition, completing the Baltic set after Lithuania and Estonia
negative_signals: Rollout 'begins soon' with no owner enablement date, the same wording used for Slovakia
Still supervised Level 2, not unsupervised autonomy
Recognition rides on the April Dutch provisional approval rather than a bloc decision
Germany, France, and Italy are still not cleared, so the 65 percent population bar is not met
A December committee vote is still only expected

key_metrics.actual: 10 EU states recognizing the Dutch provisional approval
key_metrics.target: 15 of 27 states and 65% of EU population for a bloc authorization, plus a dated owner rollout
key_metrics.trajectory: Country count up by one small state; no EU vote and no confirmed Latvian enablement

keyChanges.title: Salvini Backs a Fast EU Vote; Italy Still Has Not Approved Tesla Assisted Driving
keyChanges.description: On 29 October Italy's deputy prime minister and transport minister, Matteo Salvini, posted that he had a 'very positive and constructive' conversation with Elon Musk and that Italy supports a swift EU approval of Tesla Assisted Driving, with Musk replying with thanks. That is a large-state political signal toward the committee vote. It is not an Italian recognition of the Dutch approval, and Teslarati still lists Italy as under review alongside Germany and France. Il Foglio the same day quoted Salvini's post and reported that the Highway Code from his ministry still requires a person on board and allows trials only if they are not aimed directly at type-approval and mass production. A domestic automated-driving executive told the paper that leaves a logical block for vehicles meant to operate without a responsible driver and pushes production-aimed testing abroad. Praise for Tesla's supervised product does not clear Italian roads and does not rewrite that code.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: A transport minister's post is not Italian recognition or an EU vote. Status aligned to reality: Italy is still under review, and the Highway Code still blocks production-aimed driverless trials.

positive_signals: Italy's transport minister publicly backed a swift EU approval after speaking with Musk
Italy is a large member state whose vote matters to the 65 percent population threshold
negative_signals: No Italian national recognition and no owner rollout
Italy remains in the under-review group with Germany and France
The transport ministry's Highway Code still requires a person on board and limits trials aimed at type-approval and mass production
A social-media endorsement is not a Technical Committee vote

keyChanges.title: Tesla Japan Still Promises 2026 FSD, and Admits the Decision Is Not Its
keyChanges.description: Nikkei on 19 October published an interview with Tesla Japan president Riichi Hashimoto in which he kept a 2026 launch target for FSD in Japan. Asked about skepticism that a year-end approval is realistic, he said it is difficult because Tesla cannot do it alone, and that the company is making a maximum effort to get as close as possible to doing it '100 percent.' He tied the timing to safety and to talks with the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism and other agencies, not to a deregulation shortcut. Public-road testing in Japan started in August 2025. Hashimoto gave no date inside 2026, and Tesla did not post a matching global announcement. With two months left, 'maximum effort' is not an approval. Japanese owners are still waiting on MLIT.

keyChanges.title: Fremont Optimus called production-quality, with no count and sales in late 2027
keyChanges.description: Tesla's Q3 2026 update, posted October 21, says Optimus production began on high-volume lines in Fremont and that the bots coming off that line are the first production-quality units the company has manufactured. It also says the current process is suitable for a commercial product while hardware and manufacturing keep changing. The same deck leaves both Optimus capacity cells blank: California is Early Ramp and Texas is Construction. On the earnings call, Elon Musk said most of the equipment for a line aimed at about one million units a year is in Fremont, but reaching roughly 20,000 a week will take at least a year and maybe longer because the design is still changing. He described the start as a shallow S-curve and said the AI, the electromechanical design, and durability still have to be solved before deliveries to companies outside Tesla, which he put around the end of 2027 and limited at first to dangerous or repetitive industrial work. There is no consumer date. He said Tesla is building robots that do not have perfected hands, and that the hand remains the hard problem because a robot cannot repair itself. The Optimus Academy figure of about 10,000 to 20,000 robots is a planned self-play fleet, not a disclosed production total. CFO Vaibhav Taneja said unit cost is only trending toward the expected Cybercab manufacturing cost and gave no dollar figure. No weekly rate, cumulative output, price, or customer was disclosed. A non-scripted demo was promised within one or two months and has not been released. Musk also said an AI5 install around April 2027, if that chip stays on schedule, is part of making the robot useful.

TeslaNorth notes the reply sits under a post that also joked about a bot placing an order, so it is not a full product statement, but Tesla has published no order page. The earnings-call timetable is unchanged: deliveries to outside companies around the end of 2027, industrial work first, and no consumer schedule. A waitlist would not have been a shipment. Alaoui is the summit organizer, and he is the only named source for both the reservation window and a V3 demo.

keyChanges.title: Q3 auto revenue falls 3% and operating margin is 2.6%, with no delivery target
keyChanges.description: Tesla's Q3 2026 update on October 21 added the financials behind a delivery print that was already known. Automotive revenue was $20.56 billion, down 3% year over year. Total revenue was flat at $28.05 billion only because Services and other rose 33% to $4.61 billion while energy storage revenue fell 16% to $2.88 billion. Regulatory credits collapsed to $113 million from $417 million a year earlier. Automotive gross margin improved to 18.5% GAAP and 18.1% excluding credits, from 16.9% and 16.3% in Q2 and from 15.4% ex-credits a year ago, but operating income still fell 56% to $718 million and the operating margin was 2.6%, down 322 basis points, as operating expenses rose 39% to $4.78 billion. GAAP diluted EPS was $0.22, down 44% year over year. Teslarati's tally had non-GAAP EPS at $0.48 versus about $0.45 expected and revenue slightly under a $28.34 billion consensus. The unit math did not improve on the October 2 release: production was 464,391 and deliveries were 486,532, so about 22,100 of the quarter came out of inventory. Production of 464,391 only barely cleared the 461,974 delivery consensus. Deliveries were still down 2% year over year and Model 3/Y deliveries were down 1%, while other passenger models (not Semi) fell 48% to 8,295. Tesla said average selling price was lower, battery availability is still the limit on raising auto volume, and it again gave no numeric delivery target. The outlook says deliveries depend on demand, supply chain readiness, and how many vehicles are kept for Tesla's own fleet. A four-year-high passenger backlog and record, but unquantified, deliveries in Canada, Australia, Japan, and Taiwan, plus a record Gigafactory Berlin production quarter, are company claims without unit disclosure. Days of supply ended at 11.

keyChanges.title: US Model Y promo APR rises to 2.49% from 1.99% the day after earnings
keyChanges.description: On October 22, Tesla raised the promotional APR on most new US Model Y loans to 2.49% from 1.99% for well-qualified buyers ordering that day or later, on terms up to 72 months with at least 5% down. Rear-wheel drive, all-wheel drive, and both Premium trims moved; Performance stayed at 3.99%. TeslaNorth calculates about $10 more per month, or roughly $750 over six years, on a $45,000 loan. Model 3 rates were unchanged in this round. The six-seat Model Y L is excluded, and its Launch Series deliveries were already pushed to January-March 2027. A sales-rep note that Model 3 lease payments would rise the same night was not confirmed on Tesla's site. The move fits the backlog claim, but it is a 50 basis point trim of a rate that was 0% to 0.99% earlier in 2026, not a list-price increase. Outside the US, Tesla is still stimulating Q4: Colombia is offering 0% financing on Model 3 and Model Y for deliveries before December 31, 2026, with 50% down and a 36-month cap, and the CFO said Europe is getting extra, unspecified sales benefits.

keyChanges.title: Austin research fab still cannot make a chip; Musk floats a $100 billion bill
keyChanges.description: On Tesla's Oct. 21, 2026 Q3 earnings call, Elon Musk said the Austin research fab will start commissioning machinery in the first half of 2027 and, if things go well, make a first test chip around May or June "just to see if we can make any chip at all." He called useful volume around Q3 2028 an aspiration and told a Deutsche Bank analyst that real production would be late 2028, later than the 2Q 2028 goal the analyst cited. Capital equipment through early 2028 "is not going to be less than tens of billions," and the project will "probably be north of $100 billion" long term, but Tesla and SpaceX have not decided who pays for what. CFO Vaibhav Taneja said most orders for that first research-fab tool set are already placed. The Q3 shareholder update, posted the same day, says Austin Fab construction continued and equipment commissioning is planned for 2027. The deck photo is still a construction site, and the update does not name Terafab or fund the $100 billion figure. Musk also said fab capex "is not a massive impact right now" and only becomes noticeable, in the tens of billions, in 2028.

keyChanges.title: Korean Terafab supply talks are mostly NDAs; one R&D tool is on order
keyChanges.description: TheElec reported on Oct. 20, 2026 that Tesla and SpaceX representatives visited about 10 Korean materials and equipment companies at SEMICON West (Oct. 13-15) and that many of those talks are under NDA. The only firm equipment commitment in the report is one HPSP high-pressure hydrogen annealing system for the R&D line. Hanmi Semiconductor, KoMiCo, ISC, BMT, Unisem, and others are at the NDA, sample, or inquiry stage. Fujifilm said which chemicals would ship depends on which process technologies are selected. TheElec also says Tesla and SpaceX have not disclosed a separate Terafab legal entity or ownership structure. A starter plant of 100,000 wafers a month before 2030 is what industry observers expect, not a company milestone; the stated goal is 1 million wafers a month within 10 years. The same day, Musk posted that one building's output would rank in the top 20 of country GDP and gave no figures. One unnamed equipment official told TheElec that attempts to buy capacity from Intel, TSMC, and Micron were turned down.

keyChanges.title: Grimes County citizens sue to pry open Terafab tax-abatement records
keyChanges.description: On Oct. 27, 2026, Grimes County Citizens for Responsible Development filed in Travis County's 126th District Court (Cause No. D-1-GN-26-008509) both to intervene in SpaceX's suit to block Terafab records and to seek a writ of mandamus compelling Grimes County to release them. The request covers the June 3 reinvestment-zone and tax-abatement file: the application, drafts, and emails among the county, consultants, and SpaceX. The Attorney General ruled on July 28 that only limited attorney-client material could be withheld. KBTX and the Austin American-Statesman reported Oct. 29 that the county still has not produced the rest, and that SpaceX is still arguing trade secrets and competitive harm. Counsel Bill Aleshire estimated a hearing in December and the first orders in spring. County Judge Joe Fauth declined to comment. The petition also says the suing company should not litigate under the name SpaceX, which the group says is a registered assumed name of a different entity.
